editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. Constraint handling (one-hot and set-packing via XY-mixers, other constraints as penalty terms), "paling banyak satu titik akhir" and the benchmark notes all match the English, and the terms qubit, kekangan, pemboleh ubah and pengoptimum are used consistently. Four small things a native editor would change. "Shots" is calqued as "tangkapan", which reads as "catch" or "capture" in Malay. The benchmark claim "well above 100 binary variables" is softened to just "lebih daripada 100". Two phrases are stiff: "Apabila berkenaan dengan masalah" is a literal rendering of "When applicable", and the heading "Pewarnaan graf 3" is awkward.

examples.translation: jumlah bajet tangkapan (shot) setiap rantai
examples.suggested: jumlah bajet shot setiap rantai
examples.why: 'tangkapan' means catch or capture. It is a literal calque and not the usual rendering. The field usually keeps 'shot' as is, and the table header 'Jumlah tangkapan' has the same problem.

examples.translation: dengan lebih daripada 100 pemboleh ubah binari
examples.suggested: dengan jauh melebihi 100 pemboleh ubah binari
examples.why: The qualifier 'well' is dropped, so the benchmark claim is slightly weaker than in the English (the instances have up to 186 variables).

examples.suggested: Jika sesuai dengan masalah tersebut, masalah itu dianalisis sebagai graf
examples.why: This is a literal rendering of 'when applicable'. 'berkenaan dengan' means 'concerning', so the sentence reads stiffly.

examples.translation: Pewarnaan graf 3 (Max-3-Cut)
examples.suggested: Pewarnaan-3 graf (Max-3-Cut)

editor_note: Faithful and natural throughout, with core terms rendered correctly and consistently (expectation value→nilai jangkaan, job→kerja, primitive→primitif, parameterized→berparameter), and no drift in the Recommendations list or the batch/execution-mode passage.

The meaning is faithful throughout. The job-status list, the run() capacity checks and the note that the runtime-job list can be empty all carry over without drift. A native editor would still fix a few things. In [31], "instantiated" comes out as "dijana contohnya", which reads as "generated, for example". Some terms switch within the file: "API key", "kunci API" and "key" ([19], [25], [26]), and "kerja masa jalan" ([55]-[56]) against "pekerjaan runtime" ([57]). Two phrases are stiff calques: "memproses pasca keputusan" ([46]) and "ungkapan biasa" for regular expression ([60]).

examples.suggested: Selepas objek katalog dicipta, anda boleh memilih fungsi

editor_note: All four rewritten entries (4, 5, 6, 27) keep the English meaning and none of them would mislead a learner. There are three wording problems. In entry 6, "largely" became "secara besar-besarannya", which means "on a massive scale", so the English hedge "mostly" is lost; "sebahagian besarnya" is the correct idiom. In entry 4, "pertukaran kos dan ketepatan" is a literal calque of "tradeoff"; "keseimbangan antara kos dan ketepatan" is what a Malay technical writer would use. In entry 5, "pemprosesan pra dan pasca" is stiff; the standard terms are "prapemprosesan dan pascapemprosesan".

examples.source: these client-side primitives are largely drop-in replacements
examples.translation: primitif sisi klien ini secara besar-besarannya adalah pengganti terus
examples.suggested: primitif sisi klien ini sebahagian besarnya boleh menggantikan terus
examples.why: 'secara besar-besaran' means 'massively / on a large scale', not 'mostly'. The English hedge 'largely' is lost, which counts as a dropped qualifier (minor).

examples.source: easily configure the cost and accuracy tradeoff
examples.translation: mengkonfigurasi pertukaran kos dan ketepatan dengan mudah
examples.suggested: mengkonfigurasi keseimbangan antara kos dan ketepatan dengan mudah
examples.why: 'pertukaran' reads as 'exchange/swap', a literal calque of 'tradeoff'. 'Keseimbangan antara' (or 'tukar ganti') is the idiomatic term.

examples.source: perform most of the pre- and post-processing on the client side
examples.translation: melaksanakan kebanyakan pemprosesan pra dan pasca pada sisi klien
examples.suggested: melaksanakan sebahagian besar prapemprosesan dan pascapemprosesan di sisi klien
examples.why: Splitting 'pra' and 'pasca' off 'pemprosesan' is stiff. The compound forms are the standard Malay technical terms.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. The ISA explanation, the PUB definition, the list of execution modes and the rule that Open Plan users cannot submit session jobs are all rendered faithfully. In [6], 'largely drop-in replacements' became 'secara besar-besarannya', which means 'massively' or 'on a large scale' rather than 'for the most part'. That blurs the hedge; 'sebahagian besarnya' is the natural fix. Two smaller slips: the admonition title in [14], 'gate pecahan', should be capitalised as a title ('Gate pecahan'), and in [22] the product tier name 'Open Plan' is translated as 'Pelan Terbuka', which learners won't match against the IBM Quantum UI.

The meaning matches the English throughout, so nothing here would mislead a learner. That covers the beta caveats, the "no simulator yet" limitation, the Estimator exclusion, the per-job shots rule and the manual XOR undo of measurement twirling. The problems are consistency ones. The page addresses the reader as casual "kamu" in entries 5–80 and then switches to "anda" from entry 86 on. "Directed execution model" appears as both "model pelaksanaan terarah" (5, 19, 35) and "model pelaksanaan berarah" (80, 101). Other split terms are "results" (hasil / keputusan), "array" (array / tatasusunan), "box" (box / kotak), and "Kemaskini" alongside "Kemas kini". Also, "basis changes" became "perubahan asas", which can read as "basic changes".

examples.translation: Langkah 7. Ubah cara anda mengakses keputusan
examples.suggested: Use "anda" consistently across the page (entries 5–80 use "kamu"), and use one word for "results" (hasil, as in entries 23 and 48)

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally. Core terms are correct and used the same way throughout: shots→shot, job→kerja, noise model→model hingar, error mitigation/suppression→pengurangan/penindasan ralat. The NoiseLearner caveat in [7] survives intact ("model hingar menjadi lapuk selepas tempoh masa tertentu"), and so does the precision-versus-shots claim in [4].

The meaning is accurate throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. There are two small wording issues. In entry [6], "pull requests" is calqued as "permintaan tarik", but Malay developers say "pull request", so the literal version reads unnaturally. In entry [4], "menjadikan bahagian utama tumpukan perisian kuantum sumber terbuka" is clumsy because "sumber terbuka" trails at the end and the sentence is hard to follow. Rewording it as "menjadikan bahagian utama ... sebagai sumber terbuka" reads more naturally.

examples.source: from code in pull requests to community support on Slack
examples.translation: daripada kod dalam permintaan tarik hingga sokongan komuniti di Slack
examples.suggested: daripada kod dalam pull request hingga sokongan komuniti di Slack

examples.source: includes open-sourcing key parts of the quantum software stack
examples.translation: termasuk menjadikan bahagian utama tumpukan perisian kuantum sumber terbuka
examples.suggested: termasuk menjadikan bahagian utama tumpukan perisian kuantum sebagai sumber terbuka
examples.why: Without 'sebagai', 'sumber terbuka' dangles at the end of a long noun phrase, which makes the sentence hard to read. It is a stiff calque of 'open-sourcing'.

editor_note: Entry 19 keeps the meaning, but it renders "the reverse of the shape" as "songsangan bentuk". In Malay mathematics "songsangan" is the usual word for "inverse" (as in "songsangan matriks", matrix inverse), so a learner may pause over an "inverse of the shape". What the sentence actually means is that the tuple order is flipped, and "urutan terbalik bagi bentuk" says that plainly. The rest of the entry is faithful: "jumlah dimensi input dan output" and the Note caveat about the (input_dim, output_dim) tuple are both there, so nothing here would mislead.

examples.source: which is the reverse of the shape of the underlying matrix.
examples.translation: yang merupakan songsangan bentuk matriks asas.
examples.suggested: iaitu urutan terbalik bagi bentuk matriks asas.
examples.why: In Malay mathematics 'songsangan' means 'inverse' (as in matrix inverse). The English means the tuple order is reversed, and 'urutan terbalik' says that directly without suggesting an inverse.

editor_note: Nothing in the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entry 24 (the Disclaimer) is faithful: it keeps the hedged "boleh bergantung" and "mungkin mencapai", "selepas pascapemprosesan yang setara", and the conclusion "Oleh itu, penilaian harus mempertimbangkan keseluruhan aliran kerja pengoptimuman". The one issue is in the titles (entries 1 and 4), which translate the product name as "Penyelesai Pengoptimuman". The body of the page keeps the English name throughout ("Fire Opal Optimization Solver", "Optimization Solver Q-CTRL", "Solver"), so the title no longer matches the product name used below it. Keeping "Optimization Solver" in both titles would fix this.

editor_note: Entry 4 "QESEM: Fungsi Qiskit oleh Qedma" is faithful and natural, and uses the same "Fungsi Qiskit" rendering as the rest of the page (entries 10, 27, 84), with the anchor left unchanged.

In entry [19], "variational quantum algorithms" is translated as "algoritma kuantum berbeza-beza", which means "various/differing quantum algorithms". That removes the variational concept, and a learner would read it as a generic list item instead of the VQE/QAOA class of algorithms. It should be "algoritma kuantum variasi". There are also minor issues. "Square lattice" appears both as "kekisi segi empat" (entries [19], [28], [69]) and as "kekisi segi empat sama" (table [23]); only "segi empat sama" means square. "Feedforward" is rendered as "maklum balas hadapan" ([26], [27], [61]), which starts from the word for feedback. Entry [7] has the calque "sangat tidak remeh".

examples.source: variational quantum algorithms
examples.translation: algoritma kuantum berbeza-beza
examples.suggested: algoritma kuantum variasi
examples.why: 'berbeza-beza' means 'various/differing', so the learner loses the concept of variational (parameterized, classically optimized) algorithms.

examples.source: square-lattice surface code
examples.translation: kod permukaan kekisi segi empat
examples.suggested: kod permukaan kekisi segi empat sama
examples.why: 'segi empat' alone means quadrilateral/rectangle, and table [23] uses 'segi empat sama', so the file is inconsistent.

examples.source: classical feedforward
examples.translation: maklum balas hadapan klasik
examples.suggested: suapan hadapan klasik (feedforward)
examples.why: 'maklum balas' is the standard word for feedback, so the phrase blurs feedforward with feedback.

examples.source: is particularly nontrivial
examples.translation: adalah sangat tidak remeh
examples.suggested: agak sukar / bukan perkara mudah
examples.why: This is a literal calque of 'nontrivial' that a native technical writer would not use.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning. Entry 18 ("untuk butiran penuh tentang kelas tersebut") is faithful and natural. Entry 25 keeps the condition exactly ("tidak perlu ... jika anda menetapkan pilihan selepas memulakan primitif"). Its one flaw is "di-instantiate", a Malay prefix hyphenated onto an English verb. That is casual speech, and a native technical editor would change it to the page's existing noun phrasing, e.g. "tidak perlu dicipta sebagai instance", which matches "satu instance kelas pilihan" in entries 13 and 17.

examples.source: does not need to be instantiated if you are setting options after initializing the primitive
examples.translation: tidak perlu di-instantiate jika anda menetapkan pilihan selepas memulakan primitif
examples.suggested: tidak perlu dicipta sebagai instance jika anda menetapkan pilihan selepas memulakan primitif
examples.why: 'di-instantiate' puts a Malay prefix on an English verb with a hyphen, which reads as casual speech. The page already says 'satu instance kelas ...' (entries 13 and 17), so wording it as a noun phrase is more natural and consistent. The meaning is unchanged.

editor_note: In the level-3 row of the optimization table [7], "Unitarity-breaking passes" is translated as "Lulus yang memecahkan kesatuan". That reads back as "passed (an exam) that breaks the union". "Lulus" is the exam sense of "pass", and "kesatuan" means union or unity, not unitarity. A learner can't tell that these are transpiler passes that give up exact unitary equivalence, which is the one caveat level 3 carries. The rest of the file uses "unitari" correctly, so this row is the one misleading spot. Smaller slips: "fidelity" is rendered "kesetiaan" (loyalty), "routing" is "Laluan" (path, where "penghalaan" is the usual term), and the heading calques "in action" as "dalam tindakan".

examples.source: Unitarity-breaking passes:
examples.translation: Lulus yang memecahkan kesatuan:
examples.suggested: Laluan (pass) yang melanggar keunitarian:
examples.why: 'Lulus' is the exam sense of 'pass' and 'kesatuan' means union/unity. The concept (passes that break exact unitary equivalence) can't be recognized and the caveat is lost.

examples.source: we can calculate the fidelity between the unitary operator this circuit implements, and the exact unitary
examples.translation: kita boleh mengira kesetiaan antara operator unitari ...
examples.suggested: kita boleh mengira fideliti antara operator unitari ...
examples.why: 'kesetiaan' means loyalty. The conventional technical term is 'fideliti'.

examples.source: Layout/Routing
examples.translation: Susun atur/Laluan
examples.suggested: Susun atur/Penghalaan
examples.why: 'Laluan' means path or route. The transpiler stage 'routing' is 'penghalaan'.

examples.source: Optimization level in action
examples.translation: Tahap pengoptimuman dalam tindakan
examples.suggested: Contoh penggunaan tahap pengoptimuman
examples.why: 'dalam tindakan' is a word-for-word copy of the English idiom 'in action' and reads unnaturally in Malay.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The 50–100 qubit threshold, the angle set, the 2% depolarizing and 5% readout rates, and the Pauli-channel-only restriction all match the English. Four wording slips need a fix. In [13], "brute-force classical simulation" became "simulasi klasik secara kasar", which reads as "rough/approximate" simulation rather than exhaustive brute force; "secara daya kasar" fits better. Also in [13], the inanimate circuits are called "mereka" ("Kebolehan simulasi klasik mereka"). [7] stacks "secara cekap secara klasik", and [21] reads stiffly with "hasilnya sangat mungkin adalah 0".

examples.source: A quantum circuit on 100 qubits is beyond the reach of brute-force classical simulation.
examples.translation: Circuit kuantum pada 100 qubit adalah di luar kemampuan simulasi klasik secara kasar.
examples.suggested: Circuit kuantum 100 qubit berada di luar jangkauan simulasi klasik secara daya kasar (brute-force).
examples.why: 'secara kasar' commonly means 'roughly/approximately', which blurs the idea of exhaustive brute-force simulation.

examples.source: Their classical simulability also makes them useful
examples.translation: Kebolehan simulasi klasik mereka juga menjadikannya berguna
examples.suggested: Oleh sebab ia boleh disimulasikan secara klasik, Circuit ini juga berguna
examples.why: 'mereka' is used for people, not for inanimate things like circuits, and the noun phrase is calqued from the English.

examples.source: that can be efficiently simulated classically
examples.translation: boleh disimulasikan secara cekap secara klasik
examples.suggested: boleh disimulasikan dengan cekap pada komputer klasik
examples.why: The doubled 'secara ... secara' is stiff translationese.

examples.source: the result is very likely to be 0.
examples.translation: hasilnya sangat mungkin adalah 0.
examples.suggested: hasilnya berkemungkinan besar ialah 0.
examples.why: 'sangat mungkin adalah' is a literal calque; 'berkemungkinan besar' is the natural phrasing.
